headline: A narrow band of moderate to heavy rain from a moisture-rich Pacific storm (an "atmospheric river") crosses northern San Diego County, including Carlsbad, around 1 PM Thursday and clears the county by about 5 PM, with a slight chance of thunderstorms and street flooding, followed by dry, cool weather Friday through Sunday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: The main rain band, arriving with a weak cold front, is sweeping through Orange County and the Inland Empire late Thursday morning, reaches northern San Diego County (the Carlsbad area) and the eastern Inland Empire valleys around 1 PM, and clears all of San Diego County by about 5 PM, bringing a brief 20–40 minute burst of heavy rain and low clouds as it passes. Downpours could reach 0.50–0.75 inch per hour north of San Diego County and about 0.30 inch per hour in San Diego County, enough for roadway flooding in poor-drainage spots and rockslides in the mountains, and there's a slight chance of thunderstorms from the coast into the western valleys this afternoon, helped by ocean water still in the low to mid 70s; scattered showers linger afterward, tapering off Thursday evening to the north and overnight in San Diego County. Storm totals are around 0.25–0.50 inch for San Diego County's coast and valleys, 0.40–0.75 inch for Orange County and the Inland Empire (locally up to 1 inch near the LA County line), 0.50–1.50 inches in the mountains (most on south-facing slopes), 0.10–0.30 inch in the high desert and 0.10 inch or less in the low desert. Gusty west winds reach 25–35 mph along the coast briefly as the front passes and 45–55 mph in the mountains and deserts (Wind Advisory until 4 PM for the mountains, Apple and Lucerne Valleys and San Gorgonio Pass), weakening overnight; snow levels start at 8,000 feet or higher and fall to about 6,500 feet as the rain tapers, giving the highest peaks 3–5 inches but Big Bear likely less than 1 inch.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday is cool but drier. Another disturbance passing to the northeast brings a brief round of weak offshore (land-to-sea) breezes Saturday morning. Sunday stays cool under a weak dip in the jet stream, with the next weak system arriving sometime late Sunday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The weak system late Sunday into Monday is trending weaker and farther north, and several computer model runs (including AI-based versions) keep it completely dry, so any rain would be very light. Tuesday brings weak offshore breezes and a slight warm-up with dry weather, though highs stay several degrees below normal. Another system is possible midweek into Thanksgiving, but models disagree widely: by Thanksgiving roughly half show a weak dip in the jet stream with a chance of light rain, while the other half show weak high pressure with warmer, dry weather; either way the holiday weather should be fairly well-behaved.

coast: A northwest swell builds Thursday, raising surf to 3–6 feet with sets to 7 feet on west-facing beaches through early Friday, with strong rip currents and minor coastal flooding during high tides (Beach Hazards Statement for Orange and San Diego County coasts through Friday morning). King Tides peak next week, with tides above 7 feet possible as early as Saturday, Nov. 21. For boaters, hazardous conditions continue through Friday afternoon under a Small Craft Advisory until 10 AM Friday for waters out to 60 miles from San Mateo Point to the Mexican border, including San Clemente Island; the strongest winds and choppiest seas move through Thursday afternoon from northwest to southeast, and there's a 10–15% chance of thunderstorms on the water with the front, which could bring gusty, erratic winds, lightning and a slim chance of a waterspout. No further marine hazards are expected late Friday through the weekend.
watch_for: Heavy downpours and a slight chance of thunderstorms as the rain band crosses northern San Diego County around 1 PM Thursday, with a risk of roadway flooding in poor-drainage areas.
Mountain and desert gusts of 45–55 mph through Thursday afternoon (Wind Advisory until 4 PM).
Whether the midweek system brings light rain or dry, warmer weather for Thanksgiving.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in Thursday afternoon's rain timing and the dry, cool Friday-through-Sunday stretch, expect any Sunday night–Monday rain to be very light at most, and have low confidence in the midweek/Thanksgiving system because models differ widely.
